claims.text: Atomically dispersing Pt on a ceria-zirconia support by ALD improves catalytic activity relative to conventional impregnated Pt nanoparticles on alumina.
Atomically dispersing Pt on ceria-zirconia by ALD improves catalyst durability.
Atomically dispersing Pt on ceria-zirconia by ALD reduces platinum-group-metal consumption.
Conventional automotive catalysts typically use impregnated Pt nanoparticles on alumina supports.
Pt nanoparticles agglomerate during high-temperature operation.
High-temperature Pt agglomeration reduces active surface area and catalyst durability.
Ceria-zirconia mixed oxides offer enhanced oxygen-storage and redox properties.
ALD can produce isolated Pt atoms strongly anchored to the ceria-zirconia lattice.
Strong anchoring of isolated Pt sites to ceria-zirconia minimizes nanoparticle sintering.
Strong Pt–ceria-zirconia interactions stabilize the oxidation state and spatial distribution of Pt.
Stabilizing atomically dispersed Pt enhances catalytic turnover per Pt atom.
Stabilizing atomically dispersed Pt improves resistance to high-temperature sintering.
The proposed catalyst can maintain or improve activity at a lower overall Pt loading.

Under simulated automotive exhaust conditions from 300–800 °C with cyclic redox exposure and CO, NOx, and hydrocarbons, the ALD catalyst should improve activity per gram of Pt by approximately 15–25% relative to the conventional catalyst.
The ALD-prepared catalyst should retain a greater fraction of its catalytic activity after accelerated aging than the conventional impregnated catalyst.
The predicted improvement may become less pronounced if prolonged high-temperature exposure degrades the ceria-zirconia support.
Unusually high concentrations of sulfur-containing poisons may reduce the predicted improvement.
